newsitem.title: GEORGIA: AIOC says hopes to meet Caspian oil start-up date.
newsitem.headline: AIOC says hopes to meet Caspian oil start-up date.

text.p: The president of an $8 billion international oil consortium developing Azerbaijan's Caspian Sea energy reserves said on Monday he still hoped to meet "a very close" schedule to begin production by August 28.

"If there is good weather, we will be very close to this date," Terry Adams, head of the Azerbaijan International Operating Company (AIOC), told reporters in the Georgian capital Tbilisi after meeting President Eduard Shevardnadze.
AIOC has targeted August 28 for beginning production from its Chirag field, one of three under development in the Azeri sector of the Caspian.

Adams gave positive assessment to works on the Georgian terminal Supsa, the terminus of an existing pipeline from the Azeri capital Baku, which will help bring the oil to world markets. The line is to be refurbished by late 1998.
An existing trunk pipeline from Baku to Russia's Black Sea port of Novorossiisk will carry AIOC's first output.
Adams said finishing touches were being put on the offshore Chirag platform.
"We are very pleased with the progress we are making with the offshore platform," he said. "All the things we said 30 months ago were accomplished."

But he said efforts to lay 179 km (111 miles) of pipeline from the Chirag field to a shore storage and pumping facility south of Baku had been slower than expected because of inclement weather over the winter.
AIOC will build a new pipeline for its main production.

The consortium has made recommendations to the Azeri government on three possible routes for a new link needed to export the main output, expected to peak in 2007-10 at 700,000-800,000 barrels per day (bpd).
Two of the possible routes cross Georgian territory and a third goes to Novorossiisk.
"Georgia should be optimistic about a main pipeline route," Adams said.
AIOC is led by an alliance between British Petroleum Plc and Den norske stats oljeselskap (Statoil) ).
